items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 5:29:1
items.html: The lights that emerged from the AHP of AK are the aspects of Nefesh, Ruach, Neshama: This has already been explained in the words of the ARI above (Part 4, Chapter 6, item 6) and in what follows there; and see there in the Inner Light.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 5:29:2
items.html: The light emerging from the Einayim, etc., and her place is there above in the eye, etc., in the aspect of surrounding light. That is, the aspect of surrounding light of Yechida to ZA; but to the Nukva it does not reach at all, even from the aspect of surrounding light. As the ARI says (Part 4, Chapter 6, item 17); and see there in the Inner Light.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 5:29:3
items.html:
A scant, very fine light called sight, and it is not a complete vapour like the vapours emerging from the AHP, which are complete vapours: The reflected light that expands from above downward with the direct light within it into ten Sefirot, which is called Guf [body], is called by the name “vapour,” it emerging from a coupling by striking in the coarseness of the screen. And if the coarseness is greater, the reflected light is found greater and the level greater, as is known. And therefore, up to phase two it is discerned that the coarseness of the screen suffices to raise reflected light and draw the light from below upward in a sufficient measure that it afterward expand also from above downward to the aspect of Guf; and the reflected light is therefore called a complete vapour. But the coarseness of phase one, which is called Einayim — behold, the coarseness of that phase is very fine and weak, and it is not a complete vapour that could expand also from above downward, and therefore no light from it reaches within the Guf.
And this is what he says: and it being a fine and weak light, therefore from it were made the aspect of the vessels of Akudim, and no lights were made. That is to say, that we discern in the light of the Einayim only the aspect of the direct light in it, which is the aspect of the essence of the light that makes a coupling by striking with the lights of the AHP and brings out the vessels for them, as he explains before us. But in itself the coupling does not suffice to bring out a level of light to the Guf, as the AHP does, but only in the aspect of a weak light.
